title: The condensed ring $\underline E$ of a subfield $E\subseteq\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and $\Qlb$ an algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with the
absolute value $|\cdot|$ extending that of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $E$ be a field with an
embedding $\iota\colon E\hookrightarrow\Qlb$. Give $E$ the absolute value
$|x|_E:=|\iota(x)|$ and the topology it defines, which is the topology restricted from
$\Qlb$ along $\iota$. The condensed ring $\underline E$ is the condensed ring of
[def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring] for this topological field:

$$
\underline E(S)=C(S,E).
$$

Its underlying ring object is commutative. If moreover $E$ is an extension of
$\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $\iota$ is $\mathbf Q_\ell$-linear, then postcomposition with
$\mathbf Q_\ell\to E$ ([def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]) gives a morphism of
condensed rings $\underline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\to\underline E$
([def-sfb-padic-condensed-ring]).

proof.text: Put $a(x)=|\iota(x)|$. The identities $\iota(0)=0$, $\iota(1)=1$, $\iota(xy)=\iota(x)\iota(y)$ and $\iota(x+y)=\iota(x)+\iota(y)$ transfer nonnegativity, normalization, multiplicativity and the triangle inequality from the ambient absolute value; injectivity gives $a(x)=0$ if and only if $x=0$. Thus $a$ is an absolute value and $d_E(x,y)=a(x-y)$ is a metric. Since $d_E(x,y)=|\iota(x)-\iota(y)|$, every open ball in $E$ is the inverse image of the corresponding ambient open ball, and conversely these balls form bases. Hence its metric topology is exactly the topology restricted along $\iota$.

source.place: First two sentences: restriction of the absolute value and the resulting topology

proof.text: The ring operations are continuous for this topology: $a((x+y)-(x_0+y_0))\le a(x-x_0)+a(y-y_0)$ and $a((-x)-(-x_0))=a(x-x_0)$. When $a(y-y_0)<1$, the identity $xy-x_0y_0=(x-x_0)y+x_0(y-y_0)$ gives $a(xy-x_0y_0)\le a(x-x_0)(a(y_0)+1)+a(x_0)a(y-y_0)$. For $\varepsilon>0$, put $A=a(y_0)+1$, $B=a(x_0)$ and $\delta=\min\{1,\varepsilon/(A+B)\}>0$. If both input distances are less than $\delta$, this bound is strictly less than $(A+B)\delta\le\varepsilon$; addition uses input distances less than $\varepsilon/2$, and negation preserves distance. Also, for $x_0\ne0$ and $a(x-x_0)<a(x_0)/2$, the triangle inequality gives $a(x)>a(x_0)/2$, and $a(x^{-1}-x_0^{-1})=a(x-x_0)/(a(x)a(x_0))\le 2a(x-x_0)/a(x_0)^2$. For a prescribed $\varepsilon>0$, an input distance less than $\min\{a(x_0)/2,\varepsilon a(x_0)^2/2\}$ therefore makes the inverse distance less than $\varepsilon$. Thus inversion is continuous away from zero, so $E$ is a topological field and in particular a commutative topological ring.

source.place: Second sentence: the induced norm makes E a commutative topological ring; elementary continuity details

proof.text: Apply [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring] to the commutative topological ring $E$ constructed in steps 1 and 2. It gives the sheaf of rings $\underline E(S)=C(S,E)$ with restrictions by precomposition and pointwise ring operations, and states that its underlying ring object is commutative because $E$ is commutative. This is precisely the condensed ring in the definition.

For the conditional clause, let $j\colon\mathbf Q_\ell\to E$ be the given extension's structure homomorphism and assume $\iota$ is $\mathbf Q_\ell$-linear. Then $\iota(j(t))$ is the fixed image of $t$ in $\Qlb$, so $a(j(t))=|t|_\ell$ for every $t\in\mathbf Q_\ell$. Applying this equality to $t-s$ shows $d_E(j(t),j(s))=|t-s|_\ell$, hence $j$ is continuous. The source $\underline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ is exactly the continuous-map condensed ring of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with this topology by [def-sfb-padic-condensed-ring]. Now [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map] applied to $j$ gives the morphism whose component at every profinite $S$ sends $b\in C(S,\mathbf Q_\ell)$ to $j\circ b\in C(S,E)$, as required.

source.place: Last four sentences: Q_l-linearity implies isometry and yields the postcomposition morphism
